source.title: Thermometry of simulated Bose–Einstein condensates using machine learning
source.authors: Jack Griffiths; S. A. Wrathmall; S. A. Gardiner

record.tranche_reason: Extends the batch-size/generalization comparison to a scientific regression task on simulated Bose–Einstein condensate density profiles, reporting held-out test performance across batch sizes.
record.gate_note: Tests batch size against held-out test performance (V5). The text does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, optimizer comparisons, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Figure 5 loss curves and figure 6 error histograms are not extracted as separate results; Table 1 reports the test metric directly.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out performance across batch sizes 16–128 with Adam settings and a 100-epoch budget held fixed. This tests V5's batch-size effect in a new setting: regression from simulated condensate density images. It does not directly test image classification or language modeling.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the batch-size discussion: smaller batches generally improve held-out predictions, and the authors suggest optimization stochasticity as an explanation rather than demonstrating that mechanism. Their overall conclusion is a proof-of-principle CNN thermometry method with some transfer across geometry and thermalisation; temperature transfers better than chemical potential to toroidal traps.
record.recipe_differences: Supervised regression on simulated Bose-gas density profiles, trained with Adam for 100 epochs; reports held-out prediction accuracy rather than image-classification or language-model test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and target parameter; the reported batch-size effect is larger for temperature than chemical potential.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing convolutional features from 6/12/24 to 12/24/48 improves temperature prediction; increasing further to 16/32/64 leaves the reported accuracies unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this regression task, additional convolutional channels improve held-out temperature accuracy up to a plateau; this does not establish behavior beyond interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: The harmonic-trap-trained network transfers temperature estimation better than chemical-potential estimation to toroidal traps; average pooling and ensemble averaging lose temperature information.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transfer and pooling sensitivity depend on whether the target is encoded in bulk density or local fluctuations.

record.problems: The evidence is from simulated physical systems and a regression metric defined as the proportion of predictions within 5%, so its transfer to the image-classification and language benchmarks in V5 is limited. The table reports no uncertainty for the accuracy values.
record.rows_left_out: No required Table 1 rows omitted. Figure 5 loss curves and figure 6 error histograms were not extracted as separate rows because Table 1 directly reports the held-out metric used for V5.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Widening beyond an established zero-training-error threshold under training to convergence; no interpolation threshold is established.
Convolutional versus fully connected performance, learned local connectivity, and initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers, tuning budgets, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.

Image-classification and language workloads; recovery through longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes. The batch sweep does not locate a precise workload-dependent threshold.
Dropout, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, training–test gap rankings, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 1 values and subjects are correctly transcribed. States concern the batch-size effect, not the absolute accuracy level. Batch-16 rows are valid reference measurements but cannot establish that effect alone. Reported ties are at two-decimal precision; no repeated-run uncertainty is supplied. Batch-32 ties do not challenge V5's workload-dependent-threshold formulation. Figure 5 also shows lower training loss with smaller batches, so the study does not isolate a larger generalization gap at matched training performance or establish a sharp-minima mechanism. Figures 5 and 6 were explicitly declared omitted, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Comparison with fully connected networks and tests of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD or momentum comparisons.

Image-classification and language benchmarks; batches beyond a workload-dependent size under fixed epoch budgets; recipe adaptations such as longer training, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Temperature prediction, batches 64 and 128 versus 16, all three convolutional feature configurations, fixed 100 epochs
relationships.reason: R5/R7/R8 show accuracy falling from 0.92 to 0.82/0.73; R13/R15/R16 and R21/R23/R24 show falls from 0.96 to 0.90/0.88.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports lower prediction accuracy with larger batches across all three convolutional configurations, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Chemical-potential prediction, batches 32–128 versus 16, fixed 100 epochs
relationships.reason: R1–R4, R9–R12, and R17–R20 show only 0–2-percentage-point losses from 1.00; batch 32 ties the baseline in the two wider configurations.
relationships.display_finding: Losses of zero to two percentage points were reported, including ties at batch 32 in wider configurations, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Temperature prediction, batch 32 versus 16, fixed 100 epochs
relationships.reason: R5/R6 tie at 0.92; R13/R14 and R21/R22 decrease only from 0.96 to 0.94, so this modest batch increase produces no or small penalties.
relationships.display_finding: Unchanged accuracy or small declines at the larger batch were reported, but these comparisons remain unverified.
